evidence.description:
JGB is an American rock band led by Melvin Seals, who plays electric organ. Its mission is to continue the musical legacy of the Jerry Garcia Band, of which Seals was a long time member.

As noted in Rolling Stone, "... when Garcia passed away in 1995, and the Grateful Dead went on hiatus, Seals took charge. Under his leadership, the slightly renamed 'JGB Band' pays tribute to Garcia by performing his songs and remaining faithful to his style."

In 1996, Seals played several concerts with Jerry Garcia Band bassist John Kahn and other former members of that band. Their idea was to continue playing the same music with everyone except Garcia himself. However, Kahn died three weeks later, and Seals and the others continued without him. The membership of JGB has continued to evolve over the years.

On July 30, 2004, Melvin Seals was the first Jerry Garcia Band member to headline an outdoor music and camping festival named in honor of Jerry Garcia, called Grateful Garcia Gathering. Jerry Garcia Band drummer David Kemper joined Melvin Seals & JGB in 2007. To date, other musicians playing with JGB have included Donna Jean Godchaux, Mookie Siegel, Pete Sears, G. E. Smith, Barry Sless, and Robin Sylvester.

metadata.title: Jerry Garcia Band - Nassau Coliseum, Uniondale, NY 1993-11-01
metadata.source: Original master recording:  Sony ECM-959 stereo mic in painter’s cap, very FOB, center, on the floor -> Denon DTR-80P (master @16 bit/48khz)  DAT Transfer: Sony R-500 -> Sound Devices 722 digital input (@24/48khz)  Mastering:  Spectralayers 11 for painstaking manual scrubbing of thousands of yells, whistles, conversations, howls, yelps, laughs, etc @ 32 bit float/48khz.  Then to Adobe Audition 25.3.0.71 for EQ and fixing hundreds of small +/- 2-5db volume differences between the L/R channels due to the mic being loose in my hat — all at 32 bit float/48khz.  24 to 16 bit dithering done in Adobe Audition 2025. Tracked in CDWav 1.98.  Flac files tagged using Tag&Rename 3.9.15.
metadata.notes: Jerry Garcia - guitar, vocals John Kahn - bass Melvin Seals - organ and keys David Kemper - drums Jacklyn LaBranch, Gloria Jones - backing vocals To get to Nassau Coliseum, I had to take the LIRR from Penn Station in NYC and then take a bus from the train station to the venue. The train was extremely delayed (I believe due to a rainstorm), which caused me to miss recording the opening song "Cats Under The Stars" and the beginning of "Stop that Train". Recorded, transferred (2/12/2011), tracked (8/4/2025), mastered (5/13-8/4/2025), tagged (8/5/2025), and posted (8/5/2025) by Scott Bernstein. Taper notes: For BARN269, I am reaching back to a recording I have been wanting to release since 2011 -- my recording of the Jerry Garcia Band from Nassau Coliseum, as part of their Fall 1993 tour. I was lucky enough to see him 3 times on this tour -- the big show on Halloween night at the Brendan Byrne arena in NJ, this show the following night in Long Island, NY -- and then again almost 2 weeks later at MSG (the famous show where saxophonist David Murray sat in for the entire show). This show, the night after the big party night on Halloween was very much a sleeper show. Filled with really tasty song choices from the first note -- 2 spectacular Dylan covers, 2 killer reggae covers of Peter Tosh and Jimmy Cliff, Van Morrison, classic Chuck Berry, blues from Norton Buffalo ("Ain't No Bread..."), classic soul ("The Way You Do...") and gospel ("My Sisters and Brothers")...and just a couple of Jerry Garcia's originals ("Cats Under The Stars" and "Ruben Cherise". I just so happened to score a spectacular ticket dead center on the floor, which also happened to be an ideal location to record the show from. Everyone knows that the Grateful Dead allowed taping (at least openly since the mid 1980s), but hardly anyone realizes that in his solo forays outside of the Grateful Dead, Jerry did NOT allow his shows to be taped. So, any Jerry Garcia recordings that you've heard (Jerry Garcia Band, Garcia/Grisman, Garcia/Kahn solo shows) and are not official live releases from the band were either leaked from Jerry Garcia's vaults or "stealthily" recorded. So, in this case I decided that given my ideal recording location, I would sneak my Sony stereo mic and recently purchased DAT recorder in. The main problem with the fact that I had to be sneaky about recording is the fact that when I'm taping openly, I can put my microphones on a tall tripod and raise them up and above the fray of crowd noise. In this case, the boisterous Long Island crowd (many of whom were chemically altered) turned out to really intrude on my recording. Fans close to me loudly whooped, hollered, whistled, hooted, howled and cackled their way through the show -- which listening to this otherwise-shimmering recording a less-than ideal listen. Back when I originally transferred and started working on this recording in 2011(!), the tools that I had were much more primitive than what we have now. Trying to wipe away the loud crowd from the music was inelegant at best. Flash forward 14 years, and the tools can work a lot more "magic" on recordings that need restoration. Yes, there are many automated features that can help break out individual instruments (or vocals) from a stereo recording...and even some than claim to be able to separate audience sounds from music. Unfortunately none of that automation was helpful here. That said, I was able to listen to the entire show and painstakingly find every annoying expression of a member of the audience wipe it away from the recording -- in most cases with no trace left of the original blemish. Unfortunately this was a very slow process and it took me many weeks of slow progress to get through it all. To add insult to injury, as I worked on this recording, I noticed a somewhat constant "sway" of microphone levels going up and down a few decibels at a time between the left and right channels -- which I recall being due to a problem with the piece of duct tape I was using to keep the microphone in place in my hat, and the (stereo) mic kept moving on its own on top of my head... This channel drift was also not something which I could deal with automatically (unless I wanted to apply automated level compression to the recording to the recording, and I didn't want to do that). So this was another painstaking manual process that I took on -- for a total of nearly 3 months of actively chipping away at this recording. So, ultimately, 32 years after I recorded this incredible dark horse of a show -- and 14 years after I first started working on amazing show out, I'm excited to present this recording to you in a massively upgraded form. One warning: Jerry's voice is a bit hoarse -- especially late in the show. This version of "Reuben and Cherise" (one of his best songs) is marred by both Jerry's haziness on remembering the lyrics and his hoarseness (though his guitar playing and the rest of the band's performance on the song step up admirably). On the positive side, this performance of "Don't Let Go" goes DEEP and has an expansive jam in it. Both of the Dylan covers in this show really swing for the fences. On the whole, Jerry does a great job with the rest of the lyrics and his vocals are fine. Sadly, I was stuck in a major delay on the Long Island Rail Road from NYC on the way there, causing me to miss the opening song ("Cats Under The Stars"), but I did get my recording running pretty quickly for the next song. Enjoy! Follow me on Twitter to track my postings of FREE live music and concert photography: http://www.twitter.com/scott_bernstein Or become a "fan" on Facebook here: https://www.facebook.com/pages/Scott-Bernsteins-Live-Music-Photos-Page/166706713365451

and it has the same type of mix of all other Matrix reels I've done.  Since Garcia 
would show up at the 'Thursday night Jam' numerous times, this could be from 
late 1970 but since Merle is here it's most likely early, mid '71. There is static in the left channel but goes away and the overall dynamics are fantastic!! It's like 
you're sitting right in front of them!! As an aside Kafer's reels were destroyed in 
his parent's attic so Will's stuff is most likely the best and cleanest surviving 
analog copies.

Set 1:
--With the season of Jerome [8/1 - 8/9] nearly upon us, 
  I thought I might make a little mix and seed it.  No 
  biggie, these arent rare recordings or anything.  I do
  prefer many of these versions, and think of them as
  being well played, and extremely energetic.
  Jerry at his finest!

--This is just a fun little mix.  Ive not even bothered
  name the tracks to etree standards or anything. Also
  this is my first time seeding flac, so it is an
  expiriment of sorts...enjoy....Chris Davis [7/19/05]

Set 2:
--My first Garcia compilation seemed to be popular, so 
  here is another one.  This one, of course, is with the
  blessing of the poo...thanks for the support, my
  friend...   :)
  If the interest is there, more will follow.
  Enjoy...Chris Davis...[7/20/05]

Set 3:
--Without me intending it, this volume became a Garcia and
  Saunders compilation.  Plenty more on the shelf, so many
  songs yet to cover, but I was just in a jazzy mood.  The
  horns sound great!  Look for more in a day or two.
  Enjoy!   Chris Davis [7/21/05]

Set 4:
--This is by far the most mellow mix so far.
--Enjoy..Chris Davis [7/22/05]

Set 5:
--This started as an acoustic Garcia mix.  It transformed
  into a Garcia/Grisman mix.  I guess the other acoustic
  stuff will have to wait for another volume.
  Enjoy...Chris Davis...[7/23/05]

Set 6:
--This is the "mature Jerry" mix I talked about.  As
  usual, theres tons more I could add to this, but 
  these version are excellent!
  Enjoy...Chris Davis...[7/25/05]

Set 7:
--Obviously this is a Garcia and Guests compilation.  Some neat
  versions, and decent recordings as well.  Ive done my best to 
  accurately list the proper band titles, I hope I got it all right..
  Enjoy...Chris Davis...[7/26/05]

Set 8:
--Welcome to "Saxophone Jerry".  Some great versions, the
  sax goes so well...  The source on some of these is not
  the best sounding, but the sax work warrants the
  attention, so here it is...
  Enjoy...Chris Davis [7/31/05]

Set 9:
--I went for quality on this one.  These tracks are all
  silky.  I had to make up for missed songs, and I was in
  the mood to do a 76'er...listened to this today, and it
  sounds very nice  :)
  Enjoy...Chris Davis...[8/2/05]

Set 10:
--Outside of the Grateful Dead, Garcia spent more time
  onstage with John Kahn than anyone else.  So, I thought
  I might conclude the Garcia Compilations with a nice
  Garcia and Kahn mix. 
  Enjoy...Chris Davis...[8/10/05]

metadata.description:
Well... only took me 47 years to do this! Massive 12 hour restoration (or should I say "reconstruction") job. Hope you enjoy it! (Please leave a review if you like it)
Jerry & Merl at a small club in San Francisco. I went out for Brent's first GD show, and got treated to 2 Reconstruction shows (here & Keystone) and a solo Jorma show all in a week. Awesome! I hand held the mics for this show, sitting on the left side towards Merl. Super fun. (I was blocked from the Keystone show about a week later, but someone was perched in the back taping. Never seen that one but would love to get it!)

This show appears in 2 places here on archive, and are mis-attributed. They are both clearly from copies of my recording. One says it's a sbd, the other attributed to another taper... but you can hear the occasional mic rattle from hand holding and same audience around me. This one's an exclusive.
